headline: An arm of the Indian chemicals maker Dorf Ketal plans to spend 300 billion rupees on a 500-megawatt data center park in Maharashtra, The Economic Times reports.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a large stated investment in a major market, but unconfirmed, with no site chosen.
importance_line: Maharashtra's state government and local communities would host a very large new investment, but the report rests on unnamed sources, ET said the agreement was still to be signed, and the company has not commented.
summary: The Economic Times reports, citing unnamed sources, that Trentar, the technology and infrastructure arm of the specialty chemicals maker Dorf Ketal, plans to invest 30,000 crore rupees (300 billion rupees, as a crore is ten million) in a 500-megawatt (500 million watts) "green" hyperscale data center park, a campus of very large facilities for cloud and AI companies, in the Indian state of Maharashtra, and may soon sign a memorandum of understanding (a preliminary agreement) with the state government. Dorf Ketal did not reply to the paper's email, and an industry executive said the company is still weighing land across the state and expects to finish within about a month.
notes: Text read from the structured data of the Economic Times page (the pool's AMP link showed no text). Single report from unnamed sources. A pv magazine India headline of 6 Oct 2026 says Trentar has signed an INR 30,000 crore MoU for the 500 MW project (page blocked, not read), so the plan may have moved on; the editor may want to update this entry.
